records.numbers_detail: Cilastatin dose 200 ug/ml used in the experiments (PDF page 395, section 2.1 and 2.7); Fig. 9 on PDF page 404 shows DHP-I enzymatic activity as a percentage of untreated control with cilastatin, bar heights only, no values printed in the text
records.notes: Other pages: 403 (conclusion: 'a powerful and specific inhibitor of DPH-I', spelled DPH-I in the book), 404 (Fig. 9 text: inhibits DPH-I but not DPH-4), 405 (Fig. 10 caption). Target class enzyme is inferred from the word 'dehydropeptidase' and 'inhibitor'; the page does not say 'enzyme' at this spot but PDF page 405 says 'DPH-I, an enzyme'.

chapter_notes: Skipped 2 statements about non-receptor, non-enzyme targets (cilastatin interfering with cholesterol lipid raft internalization; cilastatin reducing cellular entry of nephrotoxic drugs). Cilastatin blocking Fas L/Fas internalization is described as a step blocked, with no agonist or antagonist role stated, so not recorded. The chapter is an experimental report on cilastatin protecting renal proximal tubule cells from nephrotoxins; the nephrotoxic drugs (gentamicin, vancomycin, cisplatin, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, paracetamol and others) are named as toxins, with no receptor or enzyme mechanism stated.
